past_medical_history: Eating disorder history (anorexia, in remission 3 years)

social_history.recent_stressor: Dissertation proposal rejection by committee 3 weeks ago; visa status contingent on academic progress; family pressure from parents in Korea

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented x4. Speaks quietly. Avoids eye contact. Highly anxious.
neurological_exam.motor: Left arm apparent weakness — 2/5 on formal testing. POSITIVE Hoover sign: when examiner tests hip extension in left leg while providing resistance to right leg flexion, left leg hip extension is 5/5. Left arm weakness inconsistent: 4/5 when attention diverted by arithmetic task.
neurological_exam.sensory: Left-sided sensory loss to all modalities, abruptly stopping at midline — clinically inconsistent (organic lesions produce graded, not abrupt, contralateral changes).
neurological_exam.reflexes: Normal and symmetric. No pathological reflexes.
neurological_exam.coordination: Normal right; cannot test left arm due to apparent weakness.
neurological_exam.gait: Left leg dragging without foot drop. Observed to walk normally in hallway when not aware of being observed.
neurological_exam.additional: No tongue or face involvement. Speech normal. Entire episode witnessed by roommate as sudden onset following phone call from dissertation committee.

patient.chief_complaint: Sudden onset left-sided weakness following stressful phone call — 2 days duration
patient.history_present_illness: Ms. J is a 26-year-old PhD student in biomedical engineering whose left arm and leg weakness began acutely approximately 2 days ago immediately following a phone call from her dissertation committee informing her that her proposal had been rejected and requiring major revisions. Her roommate witnessed the onset, describing that Ms. J went pale, dropped the phone, and immediately afterward could not use her left arm. She was brought to the emergency department. She is an international student on a student visa, and her immigration status depends on satisfactory academic progress; the dissertation rejection places her visa status under threat. Her parents in Korea are highly invested in her academic success. She has a history of anorexia nervosa currently in remission for 3 years and social anxiety disorder treated with escitalopram. She denies any headache at onset, loss of consciousness, or vision changes. She has had no prior neurological episodes. Her left-sided weakness has been stable over 2 days without deterioration. She is distressed but not showing la belle indifference.

additional_observations: Normal brain MRI with and without contrast
DWI/ADC: no acute ischemia — multiple vascular territories examined
Normal internal capsule, corona radiata, motor cortex
mri.impression: Normal brain MRI. No acute infarct, no demyelination, no structural lesion. Left-sided weakness has no structural correlate. Normal study in young woman with sudden-onset left hemiparesis. Clinical correlation recommended.

background.description: Normal symmetric 10 Hz posterior dominant rhythm.

eeg.impression: Normal EEG. No epileptiform activity or focal slowing. No EEG abnormality corresponding to left hemisphere motor symptoms. Normal study. Clinical correlation recommended.

EMG_NCS.value: Normal CMAP 8.4 mV, normal DL 3.2ms, normal CV 58 m/s
Normal MUPs with normal recruitment during covert observation — full motor unit firing noted when patient unaware of EMG monitoring

output.interpretation: Abnormal values: PHQ-9 17 score (H), GAD-7 19 score (H), Liebowitz Social Anxiety Scale 88 score (H).

additional_observations: Normal cervical and thoracic spine MRI
output.impression: Normal spine MRI. No myelopathic lesion. Left-sided hemiparesis has no structural cord correlate. Clinical correlation recommended.

FND_Physio_Response.test: Left arm strength at 48 hours of physiotherapy

output.valves: Normal. No vegetation. No mitral valve prolapse.
output.structural_findings: No patent foramen ovale on bubble study. No intracardiac thrombus.
output.impression: Normal echocardiogram. No cardioembolic source. PFO excluded on bubble study.
recommended_actions: No cardioembolic explanation for hemiparesis. Functional etiology confirmed.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Functional neurological disorder — functional left hemiparesis

differential.key_feature: MRI DWI negative at 48 hours; antiphospholipid antibodies negative; no cardioembolic source on echo; normal hypercoagulable panel; Hoover sign positive
No prior migraine history; no headache at onset; MRI normal with no cortical spreading depression pattern; no family history
No witnessed seizure; EEG normal during admission; no post-ictal confusion; onset during stressful phone call not during seizure
MRI brain and spine completely normal; no white matter lesions; CSF not tested but clinical and imaging exclusion is sufficient

optimal_actions.action: Emergency MRI with DWI — exclude acute stroke (priority #1)
Hypercoagulable panel and echocardiogram — exclude cardioembolic/thrombotic stroke in young female
optimal_actions.expected_finding: No PFO, no thrombus; normal hypercoagulable workup

optimal_actions.action: Labs including antiphospholipid antibodies, ANA (young female)
Psychiatric evaluation — identify stressors and comorbidity
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Severe anxiety, moderately severe depression, dissertation rejection precipitant

critical_actions: Emergency DWI MRI — stroke must be excluded first
Antiphospholipid antibody panel (young female with hemiparesis)
contraindicated_actions: tPA or anticoagulation without confirmed ischemic stroke — DWI is negative
Attributing to academic stress without formal FND diagnosis (positive signs required)
key_reasoning_points: In young women with acute hemiparesis, antiphospholipid syndrome and cryptogenic cardioembolic stroke via PFO must be excluded before FND diagnosis
Positive Hoover sign and improvement on distraction confirm INTACT motor pathways — functional overlay not organic damage

DWI-negative MRI at 48 hours essentially excludes ischemic stroke in most vascular territories (small lacunar infarcts occasionally DWI-negative but clinical picture and Hoover sign strongly favor FND)
Identified precipitant (dissertation rejection with visa implications) creates the specific high-stakes stressor that precipitates conversion

metadata.notes: Straightforward FND, functional left hemiparesis in PhD student. Stroke workup complete in young female before FND diagnosis.
